papers.title: A lag-aware and interpretable two-stage framework for identifying dominant precipitation-related predictors in the data-scarce Mekong River Basin
papers.whyRelevantZh: 归入“AI × 气候”：标题或摘要命中 machine learning、shap、atmospher、precipitation、hydrolog，并通过气候领域与主题关键词双重筛选。
papers.abstractEn: Study area The Mekong River Basin is a data-scarce transboundary basin where sparse, unevenly distributed, and temporally discontinuous gauge observations hinder reliable precipitation estimation, particularly under strong subregional hydroclimatic heterogeneity. Research focus This study developed a lag-aware and interpretable two-stage framework to identify dominant precipitation-related predictors across the basin. In the first stage, transfer entropy (TE) was used to preliminarily screen candidate predictors by assessing directional lagged dependence from each candidate variable to precipitation over 1–7-day lags. In the second stage, tree-based machine learning and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used to quantify predictor contributions within the fitted models and diagnose predictor structures across subregions and rainfall regimes. New hydrological insights The framework reduced a high-dimensional candidate predictor space to compact sets of 10–15 inputs. Under a common sample-based split, the compact models achieved a mean Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency of 0.232, compared with 0.275 for models using the complete preliminarily screened sets, and performed better overall than conventional feature-selection alternatives. Across subregions, cloud microphysical variables aloft and lower-atmospheric moisture variables were recurring contributors to modelled precipitation. Convective available potential energy (CAPE) and directional transport-related predictors also played important roles. In the heavy-precipitation subset (≥90 mm day−1), transport-, flux-, and energy-related predictors became more prominent in the fitted-model SHAP rankings. This rainfall-regime contrast provides a useful diagnostic of regional precipitation processes, although the heavy-precipitation results remain exploratory because of the limited number of gauge-day samples.

papers.title: The relative importance of drought-related and structural economic factors in explaining regional economic performance across Europe: an explainable machine-learning approach
papers.whyRelevantZh: 归入“AI × 气候”：标题或摘要命中 explainable、causal、climate、temperature、drought，并通过气候领域与主题关键词双重筛选。
papers.abstractEn: The European Union (EU) exhibits spatial heterogeneity in economic structure and performance, reflecting historical development trajectories, sectoral composition, socio-economic conditions, and climatic variability. Among climatic stressors, drought challenges economic resilience, particularly in agriculture and manufacturing, which are sensitive to water availability, temperature extremes, and infrastructure constraints. In this study, we quantify the contributions of drought-related and socio-economic factors to regional gross value added (GVA) across NUTS3 regions in the EU. We integrate climatic indicators from the Copernicus European Drought Observatory with socio-economic data from Eurostat, and apply an eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) model coupled with Shapley value–based interpretability methods to attribute sector-specific economic outcomes to individual features. Our analysis reveals spatial heterogeneity in the contributions of socio-economic and climatic factors to GVA. Variability in both agricultural and manufacturing GVA is predominantly explained by socio-economic factors. Agricultural GVA is influenced by the employment share in agriculture and regional area, reflecting the availability of labor and land resources, while manufacturing GVA is strongly associated with regional economic performance, as proxied by gross domestic product. Among climatic drivers, winter temperature—a factor for plant survival—explains the largest share of variability in agricultural GVA, with soil moisture and vegetation photosynthetic activity, used as proxies for productivity, also contributing. For manufacturing, median monthly maximum temperature emerges as the most influential climatic variable, with soil moisture and photosynthetic activity contributing as secondary predictors. However, these climatic associations likely reflect spatial covariation with regional characteristics rather than direct causal impacts of climate on production processes.

papers.title: Convergent coupling of latent heat with canopy greenness and divergent sensible heat baselines across alpine grassland types on the Tibetan Plateau
papers.whyRelevantZh: 归入“青藏高原”：标题或摘要命中 tibetan plateau、plateau、atmospher、temperature、radiation，并通过气候领域与主题关键词双重筛选。
papers.abstractEn: Rapid warming on the Tibetan Plateau is altering vegetation greenness and grassland composition, yet how these changes jointly modulate surface energy partitioning remains poorly understood. By synthesizing 158 site-years of eddy-covariance measurements from six alpine grassland types, we show that latent heat flux (LE; evaporative cooling) is closely associated with canopy greenness (NDVI), with a consistent slope across grassland types. This association persists after accounting for major climatic drivers and operates at spatial and seasonal scales, but is negligible at the interannual scale. Conversely, sensible heat flux (H; atmospheric heating) is decoupled from NDVI; instead, its baseline value, predicted at the mean values of vapor pressure deficit, downwelling shortwave radiation, and air temperature, diverges markedly among types, with shrubland exhibiting the highest baseline. This H baseline divergence among grassland types is spatially driven at both monthly and annual scales. This dual-control framework, comprising a convergent association of greenness with LE and a divergent ecological constraint of grassland type on H, implies that while future greening predictably strengthens evaporative cooling, shrub encroachment, by elevating the baseline atmospheric heating, may partially counteract this cooling. These findings provide empirically grounded, scale-aware constraints for parameterizing the biophysical feedbacks of high-altitude grasslands in land-surface models.

papers.title: High resolution sediment-specific surface soil moisture retrieval using Sentinel-1 time series and auxiliary data
papers.journal: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
papers.whyRelevantZh: 归入“AI × 气候”：标题或摘要命中 machine learning、shap、temperature、weather，并通过气候领域与主题关键词双重筛选。
papers.abstractEn: In this study, we examine the potential of continuous ground moisture monitoring over a mining site using a combination of in-situ soil moisture sensors and multi-sensor SAR images. We focus on assessing and improving methodologies for retrieval of surface soil moisture, i.e. ground moisture, from SAR measurements focusing on detailed in situ reference observations for several key geomaterials, i.e. sediments, typical in the study site. The mining site represents a limestone quarry located in the southeastern Finland. Our hypothesis is that sediment-specific well-calibrated models can be instrumental in improving soil moisture retrieval under different weather conditions to produce spatially explicit soil moisture estimates at high resolution compared to baseline approaches. Studied SAR data are represented by Copernicus Sentinel-1 C-band images, while auxiliary datasets include optical Sentinel-2 data. Reference data were collected using IoT enabled capacitance sensors. The reference data were calibrated based on laboratory analyses conducted on the different sediment types studied, including organic soil, clay, gravel, and flotation sand. The examined machine learning (ML) methods include XGBoost, LightGBM, random forest, support vector regression, linear regression and k-nearest neighbors. The performance of ML algorithms was evaluated using different cross-validation techniques including a five-fold approach as well as Leave-One-Sensor-Out (LOSO) to assess predictive accuracy and transferability to unseen sensors. The best performance under random five-fold cross-validation was achieved with the most comprehensive feature set which combines Sentinel-1 backscatter, time-series based soil moisture indices (SMI), Sentinel-2 optical, topographic, and temperature predictors. SHAP analysis revealed that SAR based features such as VH backscatter, traditional SMI derived from VV backscatter, and incidence angle were among the most important multi-source predictors. Adding sediment information improved Sentinel-1-only retrievals by more than 2 vol-%, but provided little additional benefit when richer multi-source feature sets were used. In the best sediment-area-level configurations, RMSE decreased to 0.037–0.050 m 3 m − 3 (3.7-5.0 vol. % points ), with R 2 values reaching 0.90. Accuracy varied by sediment texture, with the lowest errors for clay and organic soil and higher errors for flotation sand and gravel. However, LOSO validation demonstrated substantially weaker and site-dependent transferability: R 2 ranged from 0.45 to 0.67 for organic soil at a southern site and from 0.07 to 0.21 for organic soil at a northern site. Thus, high within-dataset predictive accuracy did not translate uniformly to unseen sensor locations, highlighting the need for broader spatially independent validation.

papers.title: Landscape Heterogeneity Changes and Their Implications for Agriculture in Europe
papers.whyRelevantZh: 归入“AI × 气候”：标题或摘要命中 causal、climate、heatwave、drought，并通过气候领域与主题关键词双重筛选。
papers.abstractEn: This dissertation examines the extent and implications of historical changes in landscape heterogeneity in Europe. Landscape heterogeneity is conceptualized as the combination of two complementary dimensions: landscape composition, referring to the relative abundance of different land use and land cover types, and landscape configuration, i.e. their spatial arrangement. Both dimensions can critically influence biophysical processes such as energy and water cycles, which underpin ecosystem functions and affect agricultural production. The dissertation is organized around three themes: (1) the extent and climate relevance of historical changes in landscape heterogeneity, (2) the underlying biophysical processes associated with these changes, and (3) their implications for agricultural systems. The first theme quantifies recent, widespread trajectories of change in landscape composition and configuration across Europe and assesses their potential influence on bioclimatic variables. The second theme focuses specifically on changes in landscape configuration and examines the biophysical processes through which forest fragmentation affects local temperatures. The third theme applies an agricultural economics perspective to a case study in Germany, investigating the causal effects of historical variations in landscape heterogeneity on grassland ecosystems during a severe compound drought and heatwave event. Overall, this dissertation contributes with novel evidence on the importance of accounting for both landscape composition and configuration in climate adaptation and mitigation strategies. It identifies deforestation trajectories as the primary compositional factor and forest fragmentation as the primary configurational factor affecting the ecosystem's climate-regulation functioning. Conversely, higher landscape heterogeneity in agricultural landscapes emerges as a potentially effective mitigation strategy against extreme hydrometeorological events.

papers.title: Evaluation of reanalysis datasets for studying high-elevation meteorological conditions in the Langtang Catchment, Nepal
papers.whyRelevantZh: 归入“青藏高原”：标题或摘要命中 high mountain asia、climate、atmospher、precipitation、temperature，并通过气候领域与主题关键词双重筛选。
papers.abstractEn: Climate reanalysis datasets are widely used in hydro-meteorological and cryospheric research across High Mountain Asia (HMA), where in situ observations are scarce. Here, we evaluate ERA5L, High Asian Refined Analysis (HARv2), Modern-Era Retrospective Analysis for Research and Applications (MERRA2), and Climatologies at High Resolution for the Earth’s Land Surface Areas (CHELSA) against near-surface meteorological observations between 3,865 and 5,350 m a.s.l., in the upper Langtang Catchment, Nepal, using statistical metrics and Taylor Skill Score ( TSS ). We further assess their suitability for glacier surface energy balance (SEB) and mass balance modelling. No reanalysis product consistently outperforms the others; rather, their performance varies by meteorological variable, site, surface conditions, and timescale, with generally better performance at glacier sites, likely because their relatively homogeneous surface conditions are more readily represented by reanalysis products. Near-surface air temperature ( T 2m ) and humidity (specific: q and relative: RH ) are well reproduced ( TSS > 0.77) across products, although cold temperature and both dry and moist humidity biases are pervasive across sites. Wind speed ( u ) is poorly represented across products, sites, and timescales, reflecting their limited ability to resolve boundary layer processes and local katabatic and anabatic flows. Precipitation also exhibits large discrepancies, with ERA5L and HARv2 overestimating precipitation totals by ∼89–232% and MERRA2 and CHELSA underestimating by 30%–60%. They also generate frequent wet days and early-afternoon convective rainfall, in contrast to observed late-afternoon and nocturnal-to-early morning maxima. Hourly and daily SEB simulations at the Yala-on-Glacier site driven by reanalysis forcings yield statistically significant surface melt relative to reference estimates driven by in situ datasets; however, substantial differences in magnitude exist among products. ERA5L and HARv2 exhibit relatively small errors, largely due to compensating errors between radiative and turbulent fluxes, whereas MERRA2 and CHELSA show larger melt discrepancies due to their large radiative flux errors and underestimated precipitation that affects the surface albedo. Overall, our results underscore both the usefulness and limitations of reanalysis products for cryospheric applications in complex mountainous catchments and emphasize the need for assimilation of high-elevation observations in reanalysis products, alongside improved downscaling approaches, to better resolve local-scale atmospheric processes.

papers.title: Predicting the impact of climate change on the climatic suitability for Ziziphus jujuba in China
papers.whyRelevantZh: 归入“东亚气候”：标题或摘要命中 precipitation、climate、temperature，并通过气候领域与主题关键词双重筛选。
papers.abstractEn: Ziziphus jujuba Mill. is an economically valuable tree species in China, and its climatically suitable range is sensitive to future climate risks, with implications for biological resource conservation. Species occurrence records and bioclimatic variables were integrated, and a parameter-tuned MaxEnt model was employed to forecast the potential climatic suitability for Z. jujuba in China under three shared socioeconomic pathways (SSP1-2.6, SSP3-7.0, and SSP5-8.5). The adjusted model exhibited excellent predictive performance (AUC = 0.947). Annual mean temperature, precipitation seasonality, and temperature seasonality were identified as the dominant climatic drivers. Currently, highly suitable areas (8.84% of total suitable area) are concentrated in the Bohai Rim region. Under future scenarios, although the total climatically suitable area expands across all pathways, its spatial pattern undergoes significant reorganization: contraction in southeastern margins, expansion into northwestern inland regions, and relative stability in the core area. The centroid is projected to shift continuously northwestward, with a maximum cumulative migration of 504.67 km under SSP5-8.5. Future planning must prioritize the risk of declining suitability in traditional southeastern production areas and carefully assess the practical feasibility of potential expansion zones in the northwest. These findings provide a scientific basis for climate-adaptive management of Z. jujuba resources.

papers.title: Radial growth and their responses to environmental factors of four major afforestation species after returning farmland to forest in Southwest China
papers.whyRelevantZh: 归入“东亚气候”：标题或摘要命中 precipitation、temperature、radiation，并通过气候领域与主题关键词双重筛选。
papers.abstractEn: To elucidate radial growth variation and differences in climatic responses among coexisting tree species, this study, based on 2024 monitoring data of stem radial variation, compared the growing-season phenology, stem radial growth, and environmental factors response characteristics of four tree species ( Liquidambar formosana (FX), Melia azedarach (KL), Cryptomeria japonica var. sinensis (LS), and Camptotheca acuminata (XS)). The results showed that: (1) M. azedarach exhibited the longest growing season (168 ± 9.9 days), L. formosana was intermediate (131 ± 4.04 days), and C. japonica var. sinensis and C. acuminata were shorter (117–121 days). (2) In terms of annual increment, KL1 had the highest annual cumulative increment (3.21 mm), followed by FX1 (3.18 mm), whereas C. japonica var. sinensis and C. acuminata were lower (XS2 only 0.38 mm); (3) The growth of L. formosana was primarily driven by air temperature and photosynthetically active radiation (correlation coefficients of FX2 with air temperature, soil temperature reached 0.75–0.82), while KL2, C. japonica var. sinensis , and C. acuminata were more regulated by precipitation and soil moisture. Based on these results, M. azedarach is recommended for sites with stable moisture conditions and strong soil water-holding capacity, whereas L. formosana is suitable for sunny slopes with adequate heat and radiation and good drainage. C. japonica var. sinensis and C. acuminata showed low growth but considerable intraspecific variation, and may possess survival advantages on degraded sites subject to frequent water stress. In terms of planting configuration, the approximately two-month offset in growth peaks between C. japonica var. sinensis and L. formosana suggests that mixed plantations of the two may form a complementary resource-use pattern. This study can provide a scientific basis for the selection and configuration of coexisting tree species.

papers.title: Developing 500 m‐Resolution Annual Net Primary Productivity Dataset Over the Qingzang Plateau via an Improved CASA Model
papers.whyRelevantZh: 归入“青藏高原”：标题或摘要命中 plateau、climate、temperature，并通过气候领域与主题关键词双重筛选。
papers.abstractEn: Vegetation net primary productivity (NPP) is a fundamental indicator of terrestrial vegetation productivity and carbon cycling. However, existing global NPP products may exhibit low biases over parts of the Qingzang Plateau and may not fully capture the pronounced spatial heterogeneity of alpine vegetation productivity, partly because of generalized model parameterization and limitations in representing vegetation thermal responses. To address these limitations, we developed an annual NPP dataset for the Qingzang Plateau at a spatial resolution of 500 m for the period 2001–2024. The dataset was generated using an improved Carnegie–Ames–Stanford Approach (CASA) model implemented on the Google Earth Engine platform. Key model improvements included the dynamic allocation of maximum light‐use efficiency based on annual MCD12Q1 IGBP land‐cover classes and the replacement of the traditional bell‐shaped temperature stress function with a regionally adapted logistic function as an empirical representation of temperature limitation in alpine vegetation. Comparisons with the NASA MOD17A3HGF product and the regional TPDC NPP dataset yielded coefficients of determination (R 2 ) of 0.785 and 0.708, respectively, indicating substantial spatial consistency with both benchmark datasets. The improved CASA model also produced higher NPP estimates in high‐biomass regions, particularly in the southeastern forests of the plateau. The dataset revealed a significant overall increase in NPP across the Qingzang Plateau during 2001–2024 ( p < 0.01), with mean NPP increasing at a rate of 1.94 g C m −2 year −1 . This dataset provides a transparent resource for characterizing the spatial and temporal dynamics of vegetation productivity and for supporting ecological and climate‐related assessments across the Third Pole region.
